entities.summary: Don Domingo d'Yriarte (1746–1795), a Spanish diplomat, played a crucial role in shaping the country's diplomatic relations with European powers during the late 18th century. Born into a noble family, d'Yriarte's early education focused on classical studies, which would later influence his diplomatic career. He entered the Spanish diplomatic corps at a young age and quickly rose through the ranks, serving as a confidant to King Charles IV. d'Yriarte's most notable achievement was his role in negotiating the Treaty of Amiens (1802), which temporarily ended the Napoleonic Wars and restored relations between Spain and Britain. However, his involvement in the Spanish Enlightenment and his support for liberal reforms ultimately led to his dismissal from the royal court. Despite this, d'Yriarte continued to work as a diplomat, advocating for Spanish interests abroad. His legacy as a skilled diplomat and statesman endures, with many historians noting his significant contributions to Spanish foreign policy during a tumultuous period in European history. As a testament to his enduring impact, d'Yriarte's letters and diplomatic correspondence are now held in the Archivo Histórico Nacional in Madrid, providing valuable insights into the diplomatic machinations of the time. The Spanish government has also recognized his contributions, awarding him the title of Grandee of Spain in 1795, a testament to his loyalty and dedication to the crown.
